canonical_data: a file workspace per engagement holding scope.yaml, stage state, findings, an evidence-hash index, report.md, aggregated-report.json, and validation-summary.json
current_repo_note: Reviewed at HEAD c7fb938 (2026-10-09); the LICENSE and README blobs are identical to the triage pins. The record reflects the five-state verdict taxonomy (LIKELY added since triage) and the --backend pi execution path.
strengths: Stage transitions are hard-coded recon to test to report in a crash-resumable file workspace, so the agent chooses paths and analyses but cannot reorder the engagement
Scope is enforced by configuration: the target is written into scope.yaml and a PreToolUse hook blocks any tool call outside it on every execution channel
Discovery and validation run in separate agent sessions that never share context, with majority-confirm consensus over a five-state verdict taxonomy
The 46 built-in security tools are read-only in code, with a dangerous-flag blacklist rejecting write, exploit, and persistence operations before execution
weaknesses: Strictly an authorized-use offensive-security tool: the tree ships a live AWS IAM privilege-escalation runbook and 68 skill-guided attack playbooks, and the catalog carries it only with that disclaimer
Safety is guardrail-based, so a permissive scope.yaml or modified guards widen what the agent may touch; evidence plaintext is never persisted, hashes only, which limits independent audit
Cloud-module checks run against real accounts with user-supplied credentials, and findings inherit the limits of the executing model
The verdict taxonomy and execution backends churned within weeks of review: four-state to five-state verdicts and a second pi execution backend
why_it_matters: A reference for scope-enforced authorized pentesting agents: a deterministic pipeline, configuration-enforced scope, and separated discovery and validation sessions over a read-only toolchain.
